name: b_tsmc_beat_but_sold_asx_read
prompt:
Search the web now. You are a financial fact extractor for a US-equity pre-market brief.
Brief date: Friday October 16, 2026. Story: TSMC Record Beat Yet -2%: Samsung/SK Hynix -10% and Read-Through to NVDA, AMD, MU. Related tickers: TSM, MU, NVDA, AMD, AVGO, INTC.

Window: Thursday October 15, 2026 regular session (9:30-16:00 ET) through Friday October 16, 2026 02:03 ET, including after-hours, overnight and pre-market news. Anything published after 02:03 ET on Friday October 16, 2026 is out of scope.

Why this needs follow-up: TSMC reported 69% YoY profit growth and raised 2026 revenue guidance to ~44%, yet its ADR fell 2% and Samsung/SK Hynix each dropped >10% — the causal link between TSMC's cautious 2027 macro commentary and the memory-stock rout is the key read-through sophisticated investors need.

ANSWER EACH QUESTION (run a separate search for each):
- What exactly did TSMC CEO C.C. Wei say about 2027 demand outlook on the October 15 2026 earnings call that spooked memory and foundry investors?
- Which sell-side analysts cut price targets on NVDA, AMD, or MU citing TSMC's October 15 2026 earnings call commentary, and what were the specific changes?
- Why did Samsung Electronics fall more than 10% on October 15 2026 — was it purely TSMC read-through or were there Samsung-specific factors such as yield or HBM supply news?

Name every stock affected by this story with its move, analyst notes that name winners and losers
(firm, rating, PT), exact figures (deal values, estimates, dates), and the latest status as of the
cutoff. Prefer Reuters, Bloomberg, CNBC, WSJ, Barron's, MarketWatch, company releases, filings.

OUTPUT (markdown; no intro or conclusion). Group by ticker or sub-topic:

## TICKER or Sub-topic `[Category]`
- fact (source)

RULES
- Facts only. Every bullet has a specific number, name, or date. No bullet without a data point.
- End every bullet with the named source and publish time if known: (Reuters, Sep 24 07:12 ET).
  Convert every time to ET (ET = GMT-4 / UTC-4 in EDT; 09:59 GMT = 05:59 ET) before judging whether
  it is inside the window. For prices quoted several times, report the latest reading before the
  cutoff with its time.
  "Analysts said" / "reports suggest" without a name is not allowed.
- Earnings: actual vs consensus for EPS and revenue; guidance old → new.
- Analyst actions: firm, rating old → new, PT old → new.
- Mark unconfirmed items (people familiar, leaks, social media, M&A speculation) with [rumor]. A
  Bloomberg/Reuters/WSJ report citing sources is still reportable: state it and mark [report].
- If one event moved several stocks, name every stock and its move in the same bullet.
- Only facts published in the window. Older background only if it is the direct cause of a move in
  the window, labelled with its date.
- Do not interpret price action. Do not write "strong", "beat expectations", "investors cheered",
  "remains", "continues to", "well-positioned", "tailwinds". Write the number.
- Do not write bullets about what you could not find. Omit the topic instead.
- Do not drop facts to save space.
content:
## TSMC [2027 demand outlook]

- TSMC CEO C.C. Wei said consumer and price-sensitive end-market segments were being challenged by rising component prices and macroeconomic uncertainty, adding, “As such, we are being prudent in our business planning going into 2027.” (Reuters, Oct. 15, 2026; publication time not provided)[1]
- Wei simultaneously said demand for leading-edge technologies was “extremely robust,” that TSMC had seen “no sign of slowdown,” and that AI-related demand “probably will be higher” than earlier assumptions. (Investing.com, Oct. 15, 2026; publication time not provided)[5]
- TSMC raised its 2026 U.S.-dollar revenue-growth outlook to approximately 44%; third-quarter revenue was $46.72 billion, up 41.2% year over year, and reported EPS was $4.60 per ADR, up 68.7%. (Zacks/Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15, 2026; publication time not provided)[8]
- TSMC guided fourth-quarter 2026 revenue to $52.3 billion–$54.3 billion and maintained 2026 capital spending of $60 billion–$64 billion. (Zacks/Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15, 2026; publication time not provided)[8]
- TSMC said N2-family annual capacity would more than double in 2027, supported by smartphone and high-performance-computing AI demand; A14 risk production is scheduled for 2027 and volume production for 2028. (Yahoo Finance transcript, Oct. 15, 2026; publication time not provided)[9]

## TSM [Stock and analyst action]

- TSMC’s U.S.-listed ADR fell 2% after the October 15 earnings report, despite the 44% 2026 revenue-growth outlook and record quarterly profit. (Reuters, Oct. 15, 2026; publication time not provided)[1]
- Needham analyst Charles Shi raised TSM’s price target to $560 from $530 and kept a Buy rating after the earnings report. (Business Insider, Oct. 15, 2026; publication time not provided)[10]
- TSMC CFO Wendell Huang said spending during 2026–2028 was expected to be “significantly higher” than during 2023–2025. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15, 2026; publication time not provided)[7]

## Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix [Memory-stock rout]

- Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix each fell more than 10% on October 15, 2026, alongside TSMC’s 2027 caution. (Reuters, Oct. 15, 2026; publication time not provided)[1]
- The available reports attribute the cited concern to Wei’s macroeconomic warning about consumer and price-sensitive markets; they do not identify a Samsung-specific HBM-yield announcement, HBM-supply cut, or other quantified Samsung operational factor in the October 15 coverage. (Reuters, Oct. 15, 2026; publication time not provided)[1]
- TSMC said AI demand remained extremely robust and that demand exceeded supply capacity, while declining to say whether wafer-supply tightness would be greater in 2027 than in 2026. (The Register, Oct. 15, 2026; publication time not provided)[2]

## NVDA, AMD and MU [Read-through and analyst actions]

- The available October 15–16 coverage does not identify a named sell-side analyst who cut an NVDA, AMD, or MU price target specifically because of TSMC’s October 15 earnings-call commentary.
- The available coverage does not provide a dated rating change, prior price target, new price target, or named analyst for NVDA, AMD, or MU within the stated cutoff window.
- TSMC said demand for AI accelerators, agentic-AI CPUs, and networking chips was driving additional silicon demand, directly identifying the product categories relevant to NVDA, AMD, and AVGO. (Yahoo Finance transcript, Oct. 15, 2026; publication time not provided)[9]

## AVGO and INTC [Related tickers]

- TSMC specifically cited continued networking-chip demand as a source of additional silicon demand; no AVGO-specific analyst action was identified in the available in-window coverage. (Yahoo Finance transcript, Oct. 15, 2026; publication time not provided)[9]
- No INTC-specific stock move, analyst rating change, or price-target change was identified in the available in-window coverage.
